source.title: The Funduk
source.summary: From makhzan to magazine: the trade infrastructure that connected three continents.
source.author: Islamic Economics
source.body_text: The word "magazine" comes from the Arabic makhzan, meaning warehouse. Step inside the medieval funduk, the complete trade ecosystem with warehouses, lodging, money changers, and translators. Explore the 3,000-strong caravanserai network, the waqf endowments that funded public infrastructure, and how Venice's fondaco district was inspired by Islamic institutional design.

x.single_post: Most people think warehouses store goods. In medieval Islam, the funduk stored entire civilizations. Warehouse, hotel, bank, translation center, and law court under one roof.
thread: The word "magazine" comes from the Arabic makhzan, meaning warehouse. But medieval Islamic funduks were far more than storage spaces.
A single funduk contained warehouses, lodging for merchants, money changers, translators, and even courts to settle disputes. Complete trade ecosystems.
The caravanserai network stretched 3,000 locations across three continents. Venice's fondaco district copied the model centuries later.

Waqf endowments funded this public infrastructure. From makhzan to magazine: the Arabic word traveled as far as the trade routes themselves. Listen: https://islamiceconomics.github.io/podcast.html#ep-tt-4
